core_obligations: Take the inverse image of the given submodule and get one inclusion immediately (proof lines 1644-1646).

For the reverse inclusion take a fraction in the localisation of the preimage, observe that its numerator lies in the given submodule, and rewrite the fraction as a product to conclude (proof lines 1646-1649).
proof_roadmap: Compare the two submodules using the inverse image (proof lines 1644-1646).
Rewrite a fraction as a product to finish (proof lines 1646-1650).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that every submodule of a localised module is the localisation of a submodule of the source, namely of its inverse image (statement lines 1637-1642). The proof gets one inclusion from the definition of the inverse image and the other by taking a fraction whose numerator lies in that submodule and rewriting the fraction as a product using the module structure over the localised ring (proof lines 1644-1650). The rewriting of the fraction is the step that uses the hypothesis of being a submodule rather than merely a subset. H2.
